messages:
nina: Quick announcement 1: we just released redwood-evals-tooling v1.2.0 to GitHub and PyPI. Small feature release aimed at community contributors. :sparkles:

release-bot: Release published: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-evals-tooling/releases/tag/v1.2.0 

sam: Awesome! What are the headline changes?

nina: Highlights: new example harness for multi-turn evals, CI-friendly output format (ndjson), and a contributor guide with a simple eval template. Also added an opt-in telemetry ping to help us prioritize infra work (off by default).

docs-bot: Docs updated: CONTRIBUTING.md + examples/multi_turn_harness.md.

maria: Can we include a tiny example snippet for the forum post? I can adapt it for the community announcement.

nina: Sure, use this snippet:```
from redwood_evals import EvalHarness
h = EvalHarness.from_yaml('examples/multi_turn.yaml')
results = h.run(limit=50, out_fmt='ndjson')
print(results[:2])
```

sam: Also want to call out: we added a compatibility shim for older eval configs so people won't have to rewrite their YAML. Migration notes in the release.

nina: Note: telemetry is opt-in. We added clear instructions in CONTRIBUTING.md to opt in for maintainers. No data is sent by default.

docs-bot: CI: all checks passed for tag v1.2.0 (build 8391) 6 integration tests green.

maria: I'll prepare the community post and ask @open-source-team to amplify. Can someone drop a one-liner about why this helps community contributors?

sam: One-liner: "v1.2.0 lowers the bar for contributor experiments with ready-to-run multi-turn harnesses and clear templates."

nina: Thanks. Maria 1, ping me on the draft and I'll add troubleshooting tips.

maria: Will do. Planning to post tomorrow at 10am PT. :rocket:
